To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) KBs in Canada do not rely on theories or specific models of KB; 2) they draw on a wide variety of theories and models that have been developed to support the broader field of KT; 3) evaluation of their own practice is not a priority; 4) the quality of engagement between knowledge brokers and their clients might be increased if KBs made more efforts to describe, explain, understand and evaluate the impact of their activities using theories specific to KB; and
knowledge brokers (KB) in Canada tend not use theoretical frameworks specific to knowledge broking.

KBs in this study used the Knowledge to Action framework and the Promoting Actions Research in Health Services model to guide their practice, but they did not use a model specific to knowledge broking.
